criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1. Although municipal sewage coverage statistics in Florianópolis are cited briefly as background context and the ruptured structure belonged to CASAN's wastewater treatment plant (ETE), the dissertation examines an environmental/infrastructural disaster—the January 25, 2021 rupture of the evapo-infiltration lagoon dam (LEI) in Lagoa da Conceição, subsequent flooding of 75 homes with sludge/effluent, lagoon ecological contamination/eutrophication, and post-disaster reparation controversies—rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain broad wording ('Examines a legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), Criterion 2 would be 'yes' because the dissertation examines institutional, participatory, and adaptive water governance, regulatory/environmental bodies (CASAN, IMA, FLORAM, ARESC, MPF), dam-safety law classification (Lei nº 12.334), a public civil action and judicial protection chamber, and post-disaster damage compensation rules. Under the active 2026-10-13 clarification, Criterion 2 is 'no' because none of the analysed governance processes constitute a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariffs, disconnection/enforcement, or utility regulatory structure governing service access); instead, they concern dam-rupture disaster response, lagoon ecosystem protection, and disaster victim reparation. Under both readings, the overall study decision is 'exclude' because Criteria 1 and 4 are not met.
criterion_notes.c3: Satisfies Criterion 3. It is an empirical qualitative Master's dissertation employing a single-case study design based on secondary documentary data (news reports and official documents), actor/initiative mapping through the Observatório de Inovação Social de Florianópolis (OBISF), lexical analysis (Iramuteq), controversy cartography, and 2 interviews.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4. The study reconstructs public arenas, actor vocabularies, public controversies (over flood health risks, disaster causes, dam classification, lagoon bathing quality/eutrophication, and moral/material damage compensation), and disaster governance challenges; it reports no outcome measuring household or community water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Satisfies Criterion 5 for its own research topic. Even with full-text truncation at PDF page 74 of 291, the complete abstract, table of contents, list of figures/tables, introduction, objectives, and start of the methodology chapter clearly identify the qualitative case-study design, the Florianópolis/Lagoa da Conceição public-arena unit of analysis, the dam-rupture disaster governance exposure/phenomenon, and the public-controversy and disaster-reparation governance outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Satisfies Criterion 6 (Criterion 9 in INCLUSION_EXCLUSION.md). Full text is in Portuguese, which is eligible without translation.

evidence_quotes.quote: Este trabalho tem como objetivo analisar a (des) governança da água em Florianópolis, a partir da reconstituição e análise do caso do crime-desastre do rompimento da barragem na Lagoa da Conceição e seus desdobramentos.

A Lagoa da Conceição, ator tão importante para os ecossistemas ambientais e sociais da cidade, ganha ainda mais atenção quando a lagoa e os moradores do bairro sofreram com o rompimento da barragem da estação de tratamento de efluentes (ETE).

Em vista da pergunta de pesquisa, o objetivo geral deste trabalho é analisar a governança da água a partir da reconstituição do crime-desastre do rompimento da barragem na Lagoa da Conceição em Florianópolis e seus desdobramentos.

Para operacionalização da pesquisa foi feito um levantamento de dados secundários de notícias e documentos oficiais e mapeamento, por meio do Observatório de Inovação Social de Florianópolis (OBISF), das entidades envolvidas no caso, sendo a pesquisa documental complementada por 2 entrevistas com atores envolvidos.

Como resultado, o trabalho retraça a arena pública a partir dos principais atores envolvidos, explorando também suas posições, narrativas e vocabulários além de analisar os desafios, as controvérsias, as ações e inações que performam a (des) governança da água na cidade, envolvendo atores da sociedade civil, empresas privadas, técnicos, cientistas e cidadãos que compõem essa rede complexa de atores envolvidos com a situação de rompimento da barragem na Lagoa da Conceição.

raw_response.exposure: Rupture of the evapo-infiltration lagoon dam at CASAN's Lagoa da Conceição wastewater treatment plant (January 25, 2021) and subsequent institutional, participatory, and adaptive water/disaster governance processes
raw_response.outcome: Public-arena actor networks, discursive vocabularies and narratives, public controversies over disaster causes, lagoon ecological contamination/eutrophication, and victim damage reparation, and water (dis)governance dynamics
raw_response.population_and_sample: Public-arena actors (state utility CASAN, regulatory and environmental agencies, courts, universities, civil society organizations, social movements, and disaster-affected residents) and the Lagoa da Conceição socio-ecological system in Florianópolis, Santa Catarina; corpus of news media and official documents, OBISF mapped initiatives, and 2 interviews
raw_response.rationale: Exclude (E01: Wrong topic). Although the provided PDF text is truncated at page 74 of 291, it includes the complete Portuguese and English abstracts, full table of contents, complete lists of all 53 figures and 12 tables, Chapter 1 (problem statement, research question, general and specific objectives, and chapter-by-chapter summary), Chapter 2, and the opening of Chapter 3, which conclusively establish the study's scope. This 2024 Master's dissertation is a qualitative pragmatic case study of environmental/disaster water governance following the January 2021 rupture of an evapo-infiltration lagoon dam at CASAN's wastewater treatment plant in Lagoa da Conceição, Florianópolis. It examines public-arena actor networks, media vocabularies, ecological contamination of a coastal lagoon, flood damage to nearby residences, and post-disaster reparation controversies rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (failing c1 and c4) or any rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing service access (failing narrow c2). Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study would also be excluded because Criteria 1 and 4 are not satisfied.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative descriptive-exploratory single-case study (documentary and media analysis, OBISF actor-network mapping, Iramuteq lexical analysis, controversy cartography, and 2 interviews)
